variants.headline: Assembly votes the government out
variants.sub: The government has been voted out by the Colonial Assembly.
variants.body:
The Colonial Assembly has voted the government out. It is a decisive parliamentary event, though it does not by itself describe what follows. An assessment of {target} should start with the withdrawal of confidence and avoid announcing a successor that this report does not identify.

The gazette distinguishes the Assembly's decision from speculation concerning future administrative arrangements. The removal of a government is sufficient to warrant a clear entry in the public record. It should be described without attaching unreported causes, vote totals or subsequent appointments to the decision.

The parliamentary outcome supplies the basis for scrutiny of {target}. This paper reports the loss of confidence without treating an unreported motive or future settlement as an established fact. Care in the public record is part of responsible administration.

variants.headline: Confidence withdrawn
variants.sub: An Assembly vote has removed the government in {colony}.
variants.body:
